subject: Stan Math: Jacobian bug. C++ linker errors.

messages.author: f6c60b37f22496d6
messages.subject: Stan Math: Jacobian bug. C++ linker errors.
parts:
Hi list, I am trying to use standalone Stan Math Library and I have met problems.
1.  Function jacobian in the file stan/math/rev/mat/functor/jacobian.hpp was modified in the last commit 4a4ef64febe8857d7cd0a0b9eb701103297d132a in the right direction. Now it returns conventional Jcobian and not transposed, but new bug was introduced. The line
if (i > 0)  set_zero_all_adjoints();
was replaced with the line
if (i > 0)  set_zero_all_adjoints_nested();
Here you are the test. Let's define a R2-> R3 functor:

struct test_jac_functor
{
    template <typename T>
    inline
    Eigen::Matrix<T, Eigen::Dynamic, 1> operator()(const Eigen::Matrix<T, Eigen::Dynamic, 1>& x) const
    {
        assert(x.size() == 2);
        Eigen::Matrix<T, Eigen::Dynamic, 1> y(3);
        y(0) = pow(x(0), 1./3.) * exp(-x(1) / 3.);
        y(1) = (x(0) + 5.0 * x(1)) / (pow(x(0), 1./3.) * exp(-x(1) / 3.)); // y(1) = (x(0) + 5.0 * x(1)) / y(0)
        // y(2) = x(0) * x(1) - y(0) - y(1)
        y(2) = x(0) * x(1) - pow(x(0), 1./3.) * exp(-x(1) / 3.) - (x(0) + 5.0 * x(1)) / (pow(x(0), 1./3.) * exp(-x(1) / 3.));

        return y;
    }
};
and a test function:

int test_jac()
{
    test_jac_functor f;

    Eigen::VectorXd x(2);
    x << 2.0, 3.0;
    Eigen::VectorXd fx;
    Eigen::MatrixXd jac_fx(3, 2);

    stan::math::jacobian(f, x, fx, jac_fx);

    Eigen::VectorXd y(3);
    y(0) = std::pow(x(0), 1. / 3.) * std::exp(- x(1) / 3.);
    y(1) = (x(0) + 5. * x(1)) / y(0);
    y(2) = x(0) * x(1) - y(0) - y(1);

    Eigen::MatrixXd jac(3, 2);
     
    jac(0, 0) = std::pow(x(0), -2. / 3.) * std::exp(- x(1) / 3.) / 3.;
    jac(0, 1) = -std::pow(x(0), 1. / 3.) * std::exp(- x(1) / 3.) / 3.;

    jac(1, 0) = 1. / y(0) - (x(0) + 5. * x(1)) * jac(0, 0) / (y(0) * y(0));
    jac(1, 1) = 5. / y(0) - (x(0) + 5. * x(1)) * jac(0, 1) / (y(0) * y(0));

    jac(2, 0) = x(1) - jac(0, 0) - jac(1, 0);
    jac(2, 1) = x(0) - jac(0, 1) - jac(1, 1);


    std::cout << "Analytical values:" << std::endl;
    std::cout << "y(" << x(0) << ", " << x(1) << ") = " << std::endl;
    std::cout << std::setprecision(16) << y << std::endl;

    std::cout << "dy_i/dx_j(" << x(0) << ", " << x(1) << ") = " << std::endl;
    std::cout << std::setprecision(16) << jac << std::endl;
   

    std::cout << "Autodiff values:" << std::endl;
    std::cout << "y(" << x(0) << ", " << x(1) << ") = " << std::endl;
    std::cout << std::setprecision(16) << fx << std::endl;

    std::cout << "dy_i/dx_j(" << x(0) << ", " << x(1) << ") = " << std::endl;
    std::cout << std::setprecision(16) << jac_fx << std::endl << std::endl << std::endl;

    return 0;
}
The outputs of the test function are:

if (i > 0) set_zero_all_adjoints();

Analytical values:
y(2, 3) =
0.4634990517554629
  36.6775291893564
-31.14102824111186
dy_i/dx_j(2, 3) =
0.07724984195924381 -0.1544996839184876
 -3.955419814538435   23.01335164822362
   6.87816997257919  -20.85885196430513
Autodiff values:

y(2, 3) =
0.4634990517554629
  36.6775291893564
-31.14102824111186
dy_i/dx_j(2, 3) =
0.07724984195924381 -0.1544996839184876
 -3.955419814538435   23.01335164822363
  6.878169972579192  -20.85885196430514

if (i > 0) set_zero_all_adjoints_nested();
           
Analytical values:
y(2, 3) =
0.4634990517554629
  36.6775291893564
-31.14102824111186
dy_i/dx_j(2, 3) =
0.07724984195924381 -0.1544996839184876
 -3.955419814538435   23.01335164822362
   6.87816997257919  -20.85885196430513
  
Autodiff values:
y(2, 3) =
0.4634990517554629
  36.6775291893564
-31.14102824111186
dy_i/dx_j(2, 3) =
0.07724984195924381 -0.1544996839184876
 -3.723670288660704   22.24085322863119
 -10.63751195084005   93.32874549604964           

New wersion of the jcobian function gives right values only for the first gradient.

2. There are dozens functions in the stan math library defined in a header files without inline specifier. Just one example is a function precomputed_gradients in the file stan/math/rev/core/precomputed_gradients.hpp. Even if general stan-math headers are included in different translation units a C++ linker gives an error like "duplicated symbols" or "function foo is already defined in the module bar". This might be does not make any harm for the stan library because of its architecture, but it makes difficult to use stan-math as standalone library. If I understand right a client code is made to have all its function definitions in header files and include all these headers in only one translation unit (.cpp file). This is not very convenient for every application.

Thanks

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Stan Math: Jacobian bug. C++ linker errors.
parts:
Thanks for the careful report with test. We'll fix that.
We obviously didn't have enough tests in place.
Sebastian --- can you verify and create an issue with
the test case?

I hadn't thought about declaring everything inline just
to allow definition in multiple translation units. I'd have
thought it'd blow up code size, but maybe it won't be too bad.
And we only ever build a single translation unit on top of math,
so it's never been an issue for us. It's really only the density
functions preventing us from precompiling the library rather
than using it header only. But we need to think more about
speeding up compiles.

- Bob
